{{Short description|Type o integral transform in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Hilbert–Schmidt integral operator''' is a type of [[integral transform]]. Specifically, given a [[Domain_(mathematical_analysis)|domain]] {{math|&Omega;}} in {{math|'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>}}, any {{math|''k''&nbsp;:&nbsp;&Omega;&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;&Omega;&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''C'''}} such that
:<math>\int_{\Omega} \int_{\Omega} | k(x, y) |^{2} \,dx \, dy < \infty ,</math>
is called a '''Hilbert–Schmidt kernel'''. The associated [[Integral_transform|integral operator]] {{math|''T''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''L''<sup>2</sup>(&Omega;)&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;''L''<sup>2</sup>(&Omega;)}} given by
:<math>(Tf) (x) = \int_{\Omega} k(x, y) f(y) \, dy</math>
is called a  '''Hilbert–Schmidt integral operator'''.{{sfn | Simon | 1978|p=14}}{{sfn | Bump | 1998 | pp=168}}
{{math|''T''}} is a [[Hilbert–Schmidt operator]] with Hilbert–Schmidt norm

:<math>\Vert T \Vert_\mathrm{HS} = \Vert k \Vert_{L^2}.</math>

Hilbert–Schmidt integral operators are both [[continuous function|continuous]] and [[compact operator|compact]].{{sfn | Renardy | Rogers | 2004 | pp=260,262}}

The concept of a Hilbert–Schmidt integral operator may be extended to any [[locally compact space|locally compact]] [[Hausdorff space]] {{math|''X''}} equipped with a positive [[Borel measure]]. If {{math|''L''<sup>2</sup>(''X'')}} is [[separable space|separable]], and {{math|''k''}} belongs to {{math|''L''<sup>2</sup>(''X × X'')}}, then the operator {{math|''T''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''L''<sup>2</sup>(''X'')&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;''L''<sup>2</sup>(''X'')}} defined by
:<math>(Tf)(x) = \int_{X} k(x,y)f(y)\,dy</math>
is [[compact operator|compact]]. If 
:<math>k(x,y) = \overline{k(y,x)},</math>
then {{math|''T''}} is also [[self-adjoint operator|self-adjoint]] and so the [[spectral theorem]] applies. This is one of the fundamental constructions of such operators, which often reduces problems about infinite-dimensional vector spaces to questions about well-understood finite-dimensional eigenspaces.{{sfn | Bump | 1998 | pp=168-185}}
